leads.title: Solar horizon calendar at Chankillo in the Andes
leads.why: A row of thirteen towers let observers read the date from the point of sunrise and sunset through the whole year, the earliest solar observatory known in the Americas.
leads.verify: Confirm the dating and the observing points from the excavation report, and ask whether any continuity with the Inka sun pillars at Cusco can be shown; without it generativity stays at 0.
search: Chankillo thirteen towers solar observatory Ghezzi Ruggles 2007
Inka sun pillars Cusco sucanca horizon calendar

leads.title: Geometric planetary astronomy in the Greek world
leads.why: Geometric models with epicycles and eccentrics, set out in the Almagest, were the working astronomy of the Islamic world and Europe for fourteen centuries and the framework Copernicus reworked.
leads.verify: Establish what Hipparchus took from Babylonian records and parameters (the basis for calling this derived), which parts are his and which are Ptolemy's, and the dates of the Almagest. Decide whether Rhodes or Alexandria is the better primary place.
search: Hipparchus Babylonian astronomy transmission parameters Toomer
Ptolemy Almagest date composition epicycle models
Greek geometric astronomy origins Hipparchus solar lunar theory

leads.title: Venus and eclipse tables of the Maya
leads.date: c. 300-900 CE; tables survive in a later codex
leads.why: Maya scribes predicted the appearances of Venus and the dates when eclipses were possible over spans of centuries, an achievement reached with no contact with Old World astronomy.
leads.verify: Establish the date of the Dresden Codex and how far back its Venus and eclipse tables can be traced, and the date of the Xultun wall calculations. Keep the calendar itself (Long Count, 260-day count) for a separate record under time-keeping.
search: Dresden Codex Venus table date origin Bricker
Xultun astronomical tables ninth century Saturno Science 2012
Maya eclipse table Dresden Codex prediction accuracy

leads.title: Star calendars and the Pleiades year in Polynesia
leads.date: by c. 1000-1250 CE; written down from the late 18th century
leads.why: Named stars and the rising of the Pleiades set the year, the seasons for planting and fishing, and the star paths that voyagers steered by.
leads.verify: The tradition is shared across the islands, which implies it predates their settlement; find what scholars will defend as a date and cite the earliest written records (Matariki, Makali'i, Makahiki). Keep star steering itself under the existing wayfinding concept.
search: Matariki Pleiades Maori new year history evidence

leads.title: Seasonal star knowledge in Aboriginal Australia
leads.why: Aboriginal peoples timed the harvest of eggs, tubers and fish and the movement between camps by the first appearance and orientation of stars and dark constellations.
leads.verify: The year given is only the first written record (Stanbridge on the Boorong). Establish whether any earlier date can be defended, name the peoples and the specific star-season pairings that are well documented, and avoid claims of extreme antiquity that rest on inference alone.
search: Aboriginal astronomy seasonal calendar Emu in the Sky Norris Hamacher

leads.title: Atomism in classical Greece
leads.why: The doctrine of atoms and void, preserved through Epicurus and Lucretius, was revived in the seventeenth century and fed the corpuscular chemistry that led to Dalton.
leads.verify: Establish what survives of Leucippus and Democritus and how the doctrine reached Gassendi and Boyle. Check the relative dating against Indian atomism before keeping first_known.
search: ancient atomism Greek Indian chronology comparison

concepts.name: Atomism
concepts.summary: Holding that all matter is built from minute indivisible particles whose combinations explain the variety of things.

concepts.name: Mathematical astronomy
concepts.summary: Predicting the positions of the Sun, Moon and planets, and events such as eclipses, by calculation from recorded observations.

concepts.name: Keeping the seasons by the Sun and stars
concepts.summary: Fixing the turning points of the year by watching where the Sun rises and sets on the horizon or when particular stars first appear.
